newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong pound response to strong UK economy - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Strong pound response to strong UK economy - Clarke.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday that the strength of the pound is a market response to the perceived strength of the British economy.
He made the remarks in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).

Clarke said Britain has a floating exchange rate which responds to economic fundamentals, such as healthy public finances and low inflation as well as the development and performance of its industries.

"The market is responding to the perceived strength of the British economy," Clarke said, when asked about whether he was concerned about the strength of the pound affecting British export competitiveness. He reiterated his view that the prospects for the British economy were good amid low inflation and sustained growth.
He said that exchange rates are something the British government looks at in forming its economic policy, but that it does not have a target rate.

Asked if the British economy would be able to cope with a rise in interest rates, Clarke said the economy was benefiting from his policy of aiming for an inflation target of 2.5 percent or less, which he was confident of achieving.
"I set interest rates on the basis of achieving that inflation target," Clarke said, adding that the government had got inflation "reasonably well under control" in the last few years.
Asked about a Christmas sales rush further threatening the inflationary environment, Clarke said the government looked at all relevant data and not just one set of data.
He also said December sales actually showed a slight fall.

When asked about speculation of a rate rise after his meeting with Bank of England Governor Eddie George on January 15, Clarke said that he and the governor did not prejudge such decisions. "We will look at all the data," he said.

Asked why his Conservative Party was so far behind in polls despite the good news on the economy, Clarke said the current government has brought about the best economic prospects as a result of sensible government policies.

"We're bringing home to people the risks they face, turning away from that to a party that I'm sure couldn't deliver lower inflation, couldn't deliver lower unemployment, couldn't deliver faster growth," Clarke said.
